activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Variance for Discrete Random Variables

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Variance of a Transformed Random Variable
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

$$
\textrm{Var}[aX+b] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-2$ and $b=1.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[1-2X] & =(-2)^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =4\cdot 10 \\  & =40.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.worked_solution:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

$$
\text{Var}[aX]={a}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X].
$$

In our case, $a=-\sqrt{2}.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[-\sqrt{2}X] & ={(-\sqrt{2})}^{2}\cdot \text{Var}[X] \\  & =2\cdot \frac{1}{2} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
